description: Answer job-market questions from a precomputed snapshot of current US jobs, rebuilt after each full pass over the job boards and checked by recomputing sample answers a second way. Ten ready-made questions (top employers, pay, remote share, top metros, jobs by state, top roles, new postings this week, pay transparency, posting age, employers hiring in the most states) plus a generic lookup of any metric (job count, pay 10th to 90th percentile, share showing pay, remote/hybrid/in-person shares, posting age, new postings, top employers) by one or two dimensions (title, place, company, seniority, employment type, remote), a breakdown that ranks one dimension, a negotiate question ("what salary should I ask for?" for a title, a place and an optional seniority) and a dimensions call that lists what can be asked. Cells with fewer than 30 jobs, and pay figures from fewer than 30 jobs with pay, are left out; every answer carries its sample size, as_of, a one-line method, the check result and search filters for search_jobs or count_jobs. Free.

by.description: breakdown only: what to rank (title, state, metro, city, company, seniority, employment_type or remote; place means state).

dimension.description: dimensions only: list the values of this dimension.

employment_type.description: full_time, part_time, contract, temporary, internship or per_diem (lookup and breakdown).

limit.description: breakdown rows or dimension values to return.

metric.description: lookup only: job_count, pay, pay_share, work_arrangement, posting_age, new_postings or top_employers; leave out for all of them.

place.description: US (the default), a state code such as TX, a state name, a metro area such as "Austin-Round Rock-Georgetown, TX" or a city such as "Austin, TX" (cities and metros only for lookup, breakdown and negotiate).

q.description: dimensions only: search the values of dimension.

question.description: top_employers: Which employers have the most open jobs (for a role, in a state)? pay: What does a role pay (in a state)? work_arrangement: What share of jobs are remote, hybrid or on-site? top_metros: Which metro areas have the most open jobs (for a role)? jobs_by_state: How many open jobs are in each state? top_roles: What are the most common roles (in a state)? new_postings_employers: Which employers posted the most new jobs this week? pay_transparency: Which states have the highest share of postings that list pay? posting_age: How long have open jobs (for a role) been posted? multi_state_employers: Which employers hire in the most states? lookup: Any metric (job count, pay percentiles, share showing pay, remote/hybrid/in-person shares, posting age, new postings, top employers) for one or two dimensions, such as "what is the average pay for Registered Nurses in Texas?" Takes title (or role), place, company, seniority, employment_type, remote (at most two); metric (optional). breakdown: Rank the values of one dimension by a metric, over all jobs or inside one value of another dimension, such as "which states pay Software Engineers the most?" (by=state, title=Software Engineer, sort=pay_median). Takes by (title, state, metro, city, company, seniority, employment_type or remote; place means state); one filter from title, place, company, seniority, employment_type, remote (optional); sort (optional); limit (optional, 1 to 50). negotiate: What salary to negotiate for: a title, a place and an optional seniority give the 25th, 50th, 75th and 90th percentile of posted pay, the sample size and a plain recommendation. Takes title (or role); place (optional, default US); seniority (optional). dimensions: What can be asked: the dimensions, how many values each has, the metrics, and (with dimension, and optionally q) the values of one dimension. Takes dimension (optional); q (optional search text); limit (optional).

remote.description: remote, hybrid or in_person (lookup and breakdown).

role.description: A standard job title such as "Registered Nurse" or "Software Engineer"; leave out for every job. Same as title.

seniority.description: intern, entry, senior, lead, manager, director or executive, read from the job title (lookup, breakdown, negotiate).

sort.description: breakdown only: jobs (the default), pay_median, pay_p75, pay_p90, share_with_pay, remote_share, new_7_days or new_30_days.

title.description: A standard job title; lookup, breakdown and negotiate match more than 6,000 titles. Same as role.
